{{family name hatnote|Phạm|Minh Hoàng|lang=Vietnamese}}

'''Phạm Minh Hoàng''' (born 1955) is a French-Vietnamese blogger and lecturer in [[applied mathematics]] at the [[Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology]], who was arrested in [[Vietnam]] for his political writing and activism on August 13, 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cpj.org/2010/10/a-wave-of-media-suppression-in-vietnam.php|title=A wave of media suppression in Vietnam - Committee to Protect Journalists|website=www.cpj.org|date=22 October 2010 |access-date=2016-08-20}}</ref> Phạm Minh Hoàng, who writes with the pen name Phan Kien Quoc, was convicted on August 10, 2011<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hrw.org/news/2012/12/20/vietnamese-bloggers-recognized-commitment-rights|title=Vietnamese Bloggers Recognized for Commitment to Rights|date=2012-12-20|access-date=2016-08-20}}</ref> for writing “''33 Articles that distort the Policies and Guidelines of the Party and the State''.”<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://vtv.vn/trong-nuoc/tuyen-phat-pham-minh-hoang-3-nam-tu-53319.htm|title=Tuyên phạt Phạm Minh Hoàng 3 năm tù|last=VTV|first=BAO DIEN TU|website=BAO DIEN TU VTV|language=vi-VN|access-date=2016-08-20}}</ref> He was sentenced to three years in jail and three years of probation under Article 79, “subversion of administration”—one of many [[penal codes]] defined vaguely and used to detain and arrest political activists but served only 17 months and spend another three years under house arrest.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2012/country-chapters/vietnam|title=World Report 2012: Vietnam|date=2012-01-22|access-date=2016-08-20}}</ref> Phạm Minh Hoàng was based in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam<ref name="Pham Minh Hoang">{{Cite web|url=http://viettan.org/Pham-Minh-Hoang,10185.html|title=Pham Minh Hoang|website=viettan.org|access-date=2016-08-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161014002146/http://viettan.org/Pham-Minh-Hoang,10185.html|archive-date=2016-10-14|url-status=dead}}</ref> where he used to lecture at the university and offered free classes for Vietnamese youth on leadership skills.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.loa.fm/post/141827917123/ep45|title=Episode 45 - March News Review|website=Broadcasting Vietnam|access-date=2016-08-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161011125609/http://www.loa.fm/post/141827917123/ep45|archive-date=2016-10-11|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Pham Minh Hoang"/> In June 2017, he published a call for help on his [[Facebook]] page<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/phamminh.hoang.351/posts/10207136233443405|title=Phạm Minh Hoàng|website=www.facebook.com|language=en|access-date=2017-06-11}}</ref> upon receiving the news that he is likely to lose his Vietnamese citizenship and be deported to [[France]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rsf.org/en/news/vietnam-french-vietnamese-blogger-threatened-expulsion|title=Vietnam : French-Vietnamese blogger threatened with expulsion {{!}} Reporters without borders|website=RSF|language=fr-FR|access-date=2017-06-11}}</ref> Hoang was detained by local authorities on June 23<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-vietnam-dissident-idUSKBN19E1Y4|title=Vietnam police detain dissident for deportation: wife|date=June 24, 2017|work=Reuters|access-date=2017-07-08}}</ref> before being forcibly exiled to France the following day.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/vietnamese-french-dissident-blogger-deported-france-035955200.html|title=Vietnamese-French dissident blogger deported to France|access-date=2017-07-08}}</ref>

== Background ==
Phạm Minh Hoàng was born on August 8, 1955<ref name="Pham Minh Hoang"/> in [[Vũng Tàu|Vung Tau]], what is now [[Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu province|Ba Ria-Vung Tau Province]]. In 1973, Hoàng left to study in France. Hoàng lived, studied, and worked in France for 28 years, during which time he officially joined the political party, [[Viet Tan]].<ref name="hrw.org">{{Cite web|url=https://www.hrw.org/news/2011/11/28/vietnam-overturn-democracy-activists-sentence|title=Vietnam: Overturn Democracy Activist's Sentence|date=2011-11-28|access-date=2016-08-20}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rfa.org/english/news/vietnam/professor-08102011163422.html|title=French Professor Sentenced|website=Radio Free Asia|language=en|access-date=2016-08-20}}</ref> Hoang returned to Vietnam in 2000, and worked as a lecturer at the Ho Chi Minh City Polytechnic University.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vietnambreakingnews.com/2012/10/man-gets-three-years-for-subversion/|title=Man gets three years for subversion|date=2012-10-25|language=en-US|access-date=2016-08-20}}</ref> Before his arrest on August 13, 2010, Hoàng wrote articles about political and social issues in Vietnam, which were published on his blog under pseudonym Phan Kien Quoc.<ref name="hrw.org"/> To empower young Vietnamese to become leaders and serve the community, Hoàng also started teaching free classes on leadership skills.<ref name="Pham Minh Hoang"/> Hoàng's political articles and leadership classes were the basis for his arrest in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.viettan.org/On-the-Charges-Against-Professor.html|title=On the Charges Against Professor Pham Minh Hoang|website=www.viettan.org|access-date=2016-08-20}}</ref>

== 2010 Arrest ==
When Phạm Minh Hoàng as arrested on August 13, 2010, he was detained in secret and unlawfully.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://advox.globalvoices.org/2010/09/29/hanoi-arrested-blogger-pham-minh-hoang-for-peacefully-expressing-his-political-view/|title=Hanoi arrested blogger Pham Minh Hoang for peacefully expressing his political view|date=2010-09-29|website=Global Voices Advocacy|access-date=2016-10-23}}</ref> His arrest was unconfirmed by Vietnamese authorities until September 9, 2010, when [[Việt Tân|Viet Tan]] published the details online. At the time, Hoàng was 55 years old and lecturing at the Ho Chi Minh City Polytechnic Institute. According to Hoàng's lawyer, Tran Vu Hai, Hoàng admitted to writing the essays, but did not believe he committed any crime against the state.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rfa.org/english/news/vietnam/professor-08102011163422.html|title=French Professor Sentenced|website=Radio Free Asia|language=en|access-date=2016-10-23}}</ref>

== Revocation of Vietnamese citizenship and forced exile ==
On June 1, 2017, the French Consulate in Ho Chi Minh City invited Hoàng to inform him of the Vietnamese government's decision to revoke his Vietnamese citizenship on May 17, 2017.<ref name=":0" /> Phạm Minh Hoàng stated he would be separated from his wife due to his family's situation if he were to be deported.<ref name=":0" /> Hoàng received the official letter from authorities on June 10, 2017<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/phamminh.hoang.351/posts/10207182837968489|title=Phạm Minh Hoàng|website=www.facebook.com|language=en|access-date=2017-06-11}}</ref> on the decision to revoke his Vietnamese citizenship which was signed by the [[President of Vietnam]] [[Trần Đại Quang]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://congbao.chinhphu.vn/noi-dung-van-ban-so-832-qd-ctn-23910?cbid=17870|title=Nội Dung Văn Bản 'Quyết định 832/QĐ-CTN'|website=congbao.chinhphu.vn|language=en-US|access-date=2017-06-11}}</ref> [[Reporters Without Borders]] said this was the first incident [[Hanoi]] has stripped a dissident of their nationality.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rsf.org/en/news/vietnam-expels-dissident-blogger-france|title=Vietnam expels dissident blogger to France {{!}} Reporters without borders|website=RSF|date=26 June 2017 |language=fr-FR|access-date=2017-07-08}}</ref> He was forcibly exiled to Paris on 25 June 2017 after Vietnamese police surrounded his house at night two days earlier and took him away from his home.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/06/vietnam-exiles-dissident-revoking-citizenship-170625150005282.html|title=Vietnam exiles dissident after revoking his citizenship|publisher=Al Jazeera|date=25 June 2017}}</ref> This move by the Vietnamese government was condemned by the international community with Phil Robertson from [[Human Rights Watch]] stating that Hanoi had "committed a blatantly illegal, rights violating act that deserves forceful, worldwide condemnation".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://plus.google.com/117288277289466139415/posts/CLNFwqKXNvP|title=Statement by Human Rights Watch on stripping of #Vietnamese citizenship from ...|access-date=2017-07-08|language=en}}</ref>
